text: Repairs to the Tamsin Reservoir cost 48 million, according to town officials, after a three-month project to reinforce the dam wall, replace aging pumps and upgrade the spillway ahead of the winter rains. The work, which began in March and finished last week, was carried out by Greyford Civil under contract with the Pelham Water Authority. Authority chair Nadine Kerr said the project was finished on schedule and within the approved budget. “The reservoir is now safer and more resilient for the next generation,” Kerr said at a briefing on Tuesday. Officials said the upgrades should reduce leak risk and improve water flow to nearby farms and the south district. The reservoir will reopen to visitors on Saturday.
